The transport layer (`src/tbft_transport.h`, `src/tbft_transport_udp.c`,
`src/tbft_transport_espnow.c`) hides the network substrate from the BFT
replica. Two backends ship in-tree — UDP over lwIP sockets and ESP-NOW
with on-the-wire fragmentation — and the replica (`src/tbft_replica.c`)
never has to know which is active. Backend selection is a single
Kconfig option resolved at compile time inside
`src/tbft_node.c:43-49`, and the resulting transport is owned by
`tbft_node_t` for its entire lifetime.

## Compile-time backend selection

Selection is a single Kconfig option, `CONFIG_TBFT_TRANSPORT_TYPE`,
resolved in `src/tbft_node.c:43-49`:

```c
#if CONFIG_TBFT_TRANSPORT_ESPNOW
    tbft_transport_type_t ttype = TBFT_TRANSPORT_ESPNOW;
#else
    tbft_transport_type_t ttype = TBFT_TRANSPORT_UDP;
#endif
```

| Kconfig value | `tbft_transport_type_t` | Source file |
|---------------|--------------------------|-------------|
| `TBFT_TRANSPORT_UDP` (default) | `TBFT_TRANSPORT_UDP = 0` | `src/tbft_transport_udp.c` |
| `TBFT_TRANSPORT_ESPNOW`        | `TBFT_TRANSPORT_ESPNOW = 1` | `src/tbft_transport_espnow.c` |

The enum is defined at `src/tbft_transport.h:19-22`. The public type
`tbft_transport_t` is an opaque forward-declared struct
(`src/tbft_transport.h:25`); each backend defines its own concrete
`tbft_udp_t` / `tbft_espnow_t` and casts up.

`tbft_node_init` retries transport creation up to 5 times
(`src/tbft_node.c:54-67`) because ESP-NOW is sensitive to WiFi bring-up
order — `esp_now_init()` must have been called by the host app before
`Byz_init_replica`. Each retry waits 100 ms with a log line.

## Transport interface (`tbft_transport_t`)

The interface is a flat C function set — no virtual table, since
dispatch is resolved at link time. The header
(`src/tbft_transport.h:43-94`) declares four entry points:

| Function | Purpose | Notes |
|----------|---------|-------|
| `tbft_transport_create` (`tbft_transport.h:43-48`) | Allocate + initialise backend | `mcast_ip` / `port` are UDP-only; ignored by ESP-NOW |
| `tbft_transport_free`   (`tbft_transport.h:51`) | Release sockets, queues, tasks, semaphores | ESP-NOW variant drains `send_task` first |
| `tbft_transport_set_peer` (`tbft_transport.h:63-65`) | Register a peer address | `addr->u.udp.ip/port` or `addr->u.mac.bytes` |
| `tbft_transport_send` (`tbft_transport.h:79-80`) | Send `len` bytes to `dest` (or `TBFT_ALL_REPLICAS`) | ESP-NOW fragments automatically |
| `tbft_transport_recv` (`tbft_transport.h:92-93`) | Non-blocking receive | ESP-NOW returns fully reassembled messages |

The unified address type is `tbft_addr_t` (`src/tbft_types.h:75-83`),
a tagged union holding either a `udp` (`ip` + `port`) or a `mac`
(6 bytes) field. The active arm is implicit in the configured
transport. Accessor macros are at `src/tbft_types.h:86-88`.

`tbft_node_send` (`src/tbft_node.c:103-108`) and `tbft_node_recv`
(`src/tbft_node.c:110-121`) are thin pass-throughs that also enforce
the minimum message-header size:

```c
if (n < (int)sizeof(tbft_msg_hdr_t)) {
    return 0; /* no message or truncated */
}
```

## Backend comparison

| Property | UDP | ESP-NOW |
|----------|-----|---------|
| Max payload per packet | Unbounded (lwIP MTU = 1472) | 1470 bytes (`ESP_NOW_MAX_DATA_LEN_V2`) |
| Max application message | `TBFT_MAX_MESSAGE_SIZE` (Kconfig, default 2048) | `TBFT_MAX_MESSAGE_SIZE`, auto-fragmented |
| Addressing | IPv4 + UDP port (network byte order) | 6-byte MAC address |
| Multicast | Yes — `IP_ADD_MEMBERSHIP` + `IP_MULTICAST_IF` | No real multicast — broadcast only (peer-iteration fan-out) |
| Loopback suppression | `IP_MULTICAST_LOOP = 0` | Sender self-skipped in unicast fan-out |
| Auto-fragmentation | No (relies on IP) | Yes — 4-byte header, max 32 fragments per msg |
| Reassembly slots | n/a | 8 slots, 5000 ms timeout, oldest-evict on full |
| Receive context | `tbft_replica_run()` task | `esp_now_recv_cb` in WiFi task context |
| Send context | `tbft_replica_run()` task, blocking `sendto` with 3× retry | Dedicated `tbft_send` FreeRTOS task pulling from `send_queue` |
| Peer registration | `tbft_addr_t.u.udp` | `tbft_addr_t.u.mac` + `esp_now_add_peer` (AP interface) |
| Channel | IP-layer | `channel = 0` — use whatever WiFi is on |
| Encryption at link layer | None (BFT layer authenticates) | None (BFT layer authenticates) |
| TX-queue discipline | Per-send bounded retry on `EAGAIN` | Counting semaphore credit pool |

## UDP backend

Source: `src/tbft_transport_udp.c`. Internal struct (`tbft_udp_t`) at
`src/tbft_transport_udp.c:26-36`:

```c
typedef struct {
    int sock;
    struct sockaddr_in mcast_addr;
    bool use_multicast;
    tbft_addr_t  peers[TBFT_MAX_NUM_REPLICAS + TBFT_MAX_NUM_CLIENTS];
    bool         peer_valid[TBFT_MAX_NUM_REPLICAS + TBFT_MAX_CLIENTS];
    int          num_nodes;
    int          num_replicas;
    int          local_id;
} tbft_udp_t;
```

The peer table is statically sized to
`TBFT_MAX_NUM_REPLICAS + TBFT_MAX_NUM_CLIENTS`
(`src/tbft_transport_udp.c:31-32`).

### Socket setup

`socket_open` (`src/tbft_transport_udp.c:69-181`) performs:

1. `socket(AF_INET, SOCK_DGRAM, IPPROTO_UDP)` (`:72`)
2. `setsockopt(SO_REUSEADDR, 1)` (`:80`) — multiple replicas may share
   the same port across the cluster
3. `fcntl(O_NONBLOCK)` (`:89-99`) — the BFT main loop must never block
   on I/O; a blocking socket here would hang `tbft_replica_run()`.
   The code explicitly errors out rather than silently continuing.
4. `bind(INADDR_ANY:port)` (`:107`)
5. If `use_multicast`:
   - `inet_pton` validates the mcast IP (`:116`)
   - `esp_netif_get_handle_from_ifkey("WIFI_STA_DEF")` resolves the
     WiFi STA netif (`:124`)
   - `IP_ADD_MEMBERSHIP` joins the group on the STA netif (`:143`)
   - `IP_MULTICAST_IF` pins outgoing mcast to that netif (`:151`)
   - `IP_MULTICAST_TTL = 32` (`:158`)
   - `IP_MULTICAST_LOOP = 0` (`:168-171`) — prevents the sender from
     processing its own BFT broadcasts (the "M6 fix")

`tbft_transport_create` decides whether to use multicast at
`src/tbft_transport_udp.c:209-216`. The string sentinels `"none"`,
`"off"`, and `"0.0.0.0"` (and the `CONFIG_TBFT_DISABLE_MULTICAST`
build flag) all disable mcast — the backend falls back to a
per-replica unicast fan-out.

### Multicast group and broadcast

When `use_multicast == true`, `tbft_transport_send` does a single
`sendto(mcast_addr)` (`src/tbft_transport_udp.c:288-294`) for any
`dest == TBFT_ALL_REPLICAS` request. Replicas on the same group all
receive one copy; the sender never processes its own because
`IP_MULTICAST_LOOP` is off.

When `use_multicast == false`, `tbft_transport_send` iterates
`peers[0..num_replicas)` and `sendto`s each one individually
(`src/tbft_transport_udp.c:295-311`), skipping `local_id` to avoid
wasting a TX-queue slot on loopback.

### `send_to` with bounded retry

`udp_sendto_retry` (`src/tbft_transport_udp.c:46-63`) wraps `sendto`
with up to 3 attempts separated by `vTaskDelay(5ms × attempt)`. The
intent (commented at `:38-45`) is to survive transient
`EAGAIN`/`EWOULDBLOCK` from a momentarily-full WiFi MAC or lwIP TX
queue, which previously caused "only one replica's reply reaches the
client" under burst load. Hard errors (e.g. `ENETUNREACH`) return
immediately.

### `recv_from` and sender identification

`tbft_transport_recv` (`src/tbft_transport_udp.c:331-368`) uses
`recvfrom` non-blocking. On `EAGAIN`/`EWOULDBLOCK` it returns `0`
immediately — the previous `vTaskDelay(10)` cap that limited the
BFT main loop to 100 receives/sec has been removed (the "HIGH FIX
H4" comment at `:344-348`).

When the caller passes a non-NULL `src_id`, the backend walks the
peer table and matches the incoming IPv4:port against
`tbft_addr_udp_ip / tbft_addr_udp_port` (`tbft_transport_udp.c:355-365`).
A miss yields `*src_id = -1`.

### Address resolution and `local_id` autodetect

`tbft_transport_set_peer` (`src/tbft_transport_udp.c:257-280`) stores
the peer address and then queries the WiFi STA netif IP. If the
peer IP equals the local IP, `local_id` is set to that node id
(`:273-278`). This mirrors the ESP-NOW backend's eFuse-MAC check
and is used by the broadcast-unicast fallback to skip
`sendto`-to-self via UDP loopback.

## ESP-NOW backend

Source: `src/tbft_transport_espnow.c`. Internal struct
(`tbft_espnow_t`) at `src/tbft_transport_espnow.c:122-142`:

```c
typedef struct tbft_espnow {
    tbft_addr_t  peers[TBFT_MAX_NUM_REPLICAS + TBFT_MAX_NUM_CLIENTS];
    bool         peer_valid[TBFT_MAX_NUM_REPLICAS + TBFT_MAX_NUM_CLIENTS];
    uint8_t      peer_ap_mac[TBFT_MAX_NUM_REPLICAS + TBFT_MAX_NUM_CLIENTS][6];
    int          num_nodes;
    int          num_replicas;
    int          local_id;

    QueueHandle_t     msg_queue;     /* reassembled msgs to replica loop */
    QueueHandle_t     send_queue;    /* raw sends to send_task          */
    TaskHandle_t      send_task_handle;
    SemaphoreHandle_t task_exit_sem;

    reasm_slot_t  reasm[REASM_MAX_SLOTS];  /* 8 slots               */
    uint16_t      next_msg_id;
    SemaphoreHandle_t lock;
    volatile bool reasm_stale_flag;
    volatile bool shutting_down;
    SemaphoreHandle_t send_credit_sem;     /* counting semaphore   */
    TickType_t     last_fail_tick[TBFT_MAX_NUM_REPLICAS + TBFT_MAX_NUM_CLIENTS];
} tbft_espnow_t;
```

### Lifecycle and singleton guard

`tbft_transport_create` (`:600-684`) refuses a second instance
(`g_espnow_ctx` already non-NULL → error, `:601-604`). The
allocation order at `:627-631` deliberately creates the large queues
first to avoid heap fragmentation, then installs the singleton
context, registers callbacks, and finally spawns the send task
(`:665`). `g_espnow_ctx` is the pointer used by both ESP-NOW
callbacks to reach struct state without a public lookup function.

`tbft_transport_free` (`:686-716`) sets `shutting_down = true`,
unregisters the ESP-NOW callbacks, drops the global pointer, waits
50 ms (`vTaskDelay(pdMS_TO_TICKS(50))`, `:695`), enqueues a
`SEND_TASK_SHUTDOWN` sentinel, waits up to 1 s for the send task to
drain via `task_exit_sem`, and force-deletes if it does not exit
cleanly.

### Receive path (`espnow_recv_cb`)

Registered via `esp_now_register_recv_cb(espnow_recv_cb)`
(`tbft_transport_espnow.c:650`). Runs in the **WiFi task context**,
not an ISR (the BFT `espnow_recv_cb` and `espnow_send_cb` use
standard task-context FreeRTOS APIs: `xSemaphoreTake`, `xQueueSend`,
`vTaskDelay`). The callback short-circuits on any fragment shorter
than `sizeof(frag_hdr_t)` (`:339`) and otherwise:

1. Takes the reasm mutex with a 5 ms timeout
   (`pdMS_TO_TICKS(5)`, `:356`). The "HIGH FIX H1" comment at
   `:352-355` explains: if the lock is contended the callback drops
   the fragment — BFT already tolerates loss, and Espressif docs
   warn against lengthy work in WiFi callbacks.
2. Calls `reasm_clear_stale` (`:364`) to free timed-out slots.
3. Resolves / allocates a slot via `reasm_find_or_alloc` (`:367`).
4. Calls `reasm_feed` (`:376`) to insert the fragment. On
   completion it copies the reassembled buffer out of the slot
   **before** releasing the lock (`:381-385`), so the slot is
   immediately reusable for the next message.
5. Marks the slot stale and sets `reasm_stale_flag`
   (`:387-388`).
6. Releases the mutex, then `xQueueSend` to `msg_queue` non-blocking
   (`:394`). If the queue is full the message is dropped (with a
   rate-limited log for replies destined for clients).

The first byte of every BFT message is `tbft_msg_hdr_t.tag`; the
callback peeks at it (`:385`) only to choose the log level when the
queue is full.

### Send path and `espnow_send_task`

`tbft_transport_send` (`:766-790`) is non-blocking: it copies the
message into a `send_entry_t` and `xQueueSend`s to `send_queue` with
a 100 ms timeout (`SEND_QUEUE_TIMEOUT_MS`, `:785`). If the queue is
full the send is dropped with a warning. The `shutting_down` flag
short-circuits returns early (`:768-772`).

`espnow_send_task` (`:501-577`) is a dedicated FreeRTOS task with
8 KB stack and priority 5 (`SEND_TASK_STACK_SIZE`,
`SEND_TASK_PRIORITY`, defined at `:53-54`). It:

1. Blocks on `send_queue` for `SEND_TASK_RECV_TIMEOUT_MS = 50 ms`
   (`:506`). On timeout it opportunistically clears stale reassembly
   slots if `reasm_stale_flag` is set, then loops.
2. Honours the `SEND_TASK_SHUTDOWN = -999` sentinel
   (`tbft_transport_espnow.c:73`) by clearing stale slots, giving
   `task_exit_sem`, and deleting itself (`:522-531`).
3. For `TBFT_ALL_REPLICAS` (`:533-559`): assigns one
   `next_msg_id` per logical message (`:540-543`), then iterates
   `peers[0..num_replicas)` skipping `local_id` and unregistered
   peers. Each call to `espnow_do_send` returns the number of bytes
   accepted by the ESP-NOW driver.
4. For a specific `dest` (`:560-575`): assigns a fresh `msg_id` and
   forwards to `espnow_do_send`.

### Auto-fragmentation

ESP-NOW v2.0 caps a single packet at 1470 bytes
(`ESPNOW_MAX_DATA_LEN = ESP_NOW_MAX_DATA_LEN_V2`,
`tbft_transport_espnow.c:35-37`). For BFT messages that exceed this
limit, `espnow_do_send` (`:415-499`) prepends a 4-byte `frag_hdr_t`
(`src/tbft_transport_espnow.c:88-93`) to every packet:

```c
#pragma pack(push, 1)
typedef struct {
    uint16_t msg_id;     /* logical message id assigned by send_task     */
    uint8_t  frag_idx;   /* 0-based index of this fragment              */
    uint8_t  frag_total; /* total number of fragments in this message   */
} frag_hdr_t;
#pragma pack(pop)
```

Max payload per fragment is therefore:

```
FRAG_MAX_PAYLOAD = ESPNOW_MAX_DATA_LEN - FRAG_HDR_SIZE = 1470 - 4 = 1466
```

The 4 KB example (4,000 bytes) splits into 3 fragments as follows:

```
+--------------------+--------------------+--------------------+
|      Fragment 0    |      Fragment 1    |      Fragment 2    |
|   msg_id=X, idx=0, |   msg_id=X, idx=1, |   msg_id=X, idx=2, |
|   total=3, 1466B   |   total=3, 1466B   |   total=3, 1068B   |
+--------------------+--------------------+--------------------+
| ^ 4-byte frag_hdr precedes every fragment                       |
+---------------------------------------------------------------+
  total bytes on wire: 3 × (4 + ~1466) = ~4410
```

The single-fragment fast path lives at `:434-457`: if
`len + sizeof(frag_hdr_t) <= ESPNOW_MAX_DATA_LEN` the whole message
goes in one `esp_now_send` with `frag_total = 1`. The multi-fragment
loop starts at `:460-497`: it computes `frag_total` as a `uint8_t`
ceiling division, writes a fresh `frag_hdr_t` per chunk, and calls
`esp_now_send` per fragment. A `_Static_assert` at `:97-98` caps
`FRAG_MAX_PARTS` at 32 to fit the 32-bit `frag_mask` in
`reasm_slot_t` (`:114`).

`espnow_do_send` retries each fragment up to `MAX_RETRIES = 2`
times with `FRAG_INTER_DELAY_MS = 20` ms backoff
(`tbft_transport_espnow.c:44`). Each attempt takes a credit from
`send_credit_sem` (`:441`, `:476`) and releases it on
`esp_now_send != ESP_OK` to keep the semaphore balanced.

The transmitter's per-peer `last_fail_tick[]` (`:141`) is set by
`espnow_send_cb` on every `ESP_NOW_SEND_FAIL` (`:328`) and cleared
on success. `espnow_do_send` consults it (`:418-425`) and refuses
to send for 1000 ms after a recent failure — this is a soft
"offline" cooldown to avoid hammering a peer whose link is broken.

### Reassembly slots and timeouts

`reasm_slot_t` (`src/tbft_transport_espnow.c:108-120`) holds:

| Field | Purpose |
|-------|---------|
| `buf[TBFT_MAX_MESSAGE_SIZE]` | Reassembled message buffer |
| `buf_len` | Total bytes when complete |
| `msg_id`, `frag_total` | Match incoming fragments |
| `frag_received` | Count of distinct frags received |
| `frag_mask` (uint32_t) | Set bits = received frag indices (max 32) |
| `src_mac[6]` | Sender MAC — slots are per (msg_id, src_mac) |
| `valid`, `stale` | Lifecycle flags |
| `last_tick` | Used for timeout (`REASM_TIMEOUT_MS = 5000`) |
| `last_frag_len` | Length of the final fragment (used at `:295`) |

There are `REASM_MAX_SLOTS = 8` slots (`tbft_transport_espnow.c:42`).
`reasm_find_or_alloc` (`:192-242`):

1. Returns an existing slot matching `msg_id` + `src_mac`.
2. Returns the first slot with `!valid` (fresh allocation).
3. Returns the first slot whose `last_tick` is older than
   `REASM_TIMEOUT_MS` (timeout eviction).
4. If all slots are full and non-stale, evicts the oldest
   (`last_tick`-minimum) — emitting a warning at `:233-237` so
   operators can spot undersized `REASM_MAX_SLOTS`.

`reasm_feed` (`:244-299`) writes the payload at
`offset = frag_idx * FRAG_MAX_PAYLOAD` and sets the corresponding
bit in `frag_mask`. Duplicate fragments (bit already set) are
silently dropped at `:271-275`. Bounds check at `:278-283`
rejects any fragment that would push the buffer past
`TBFT_MAX_MESSAGE_SIZE`.

### TX credits and concurrency control

`ESPNOW_TX_CREDITS` is a counting semaphore
(`xSemaphoreCreateCounting`, `tbft_transport_espnow.c:631`). Its
capacity is the lesser of `TBFT_MAX_NUM_REPLICAS - 1` and a
compile-time cap of 6 (`ESPNOW_CREDITS_CAP`, `:64-70`). The comment
at `:58-63` explains: the ESP-NOW driver is a precompiled blob
without a documented internal queue size; 6 keeps the driver below
its undocumented limit, and because credits are taken per-fragment
(not pre-acquired) a 2-fragment broadcast to 6 peers fits. Each
successful send releases one credit in `espnow_send_cb` (`:333`).
Acquisition is bounded by `ESPNOW_CREDIT_TIMEOUT_MS = 100`
(`tbft_transport_espnow.c:71`).

### Peer registration and AP-vs-base MAC

ESP-NOW is normally addressed by the **AP interface MAC** because
that's the interface used for sending (`WIFI_IF_AP`,
`tbft_transport_espnow.c:756`). The BFT config file, however, lists
the **eFuse (STA base) MAC** of every peer. `get_ap_mac`
(`tbft_transport_espnow.c:150-156`) increments the last byte of the
base MAC, carrying carry through higher bytes, to derive the AP
MAC. `get_base_mac` (`:158-165`) is the inverse and is used when
matching an incoming `src_addr` (which is the AP MAC) back to a
configured node id (`find_node_by_mac`, `:579-594`).

`tbft_transport_set_peer` (`:718-764`):

1. Stores the peer address (`peers[]` + `peer_valid[]`).
2. Caches the derived AP MAC in `peer_ap_mac[]` (`:727`) — the
   hot send path reads this without re-deriving.
3. Compares the base MAC against `esp_efuse_mac_get_default()` to
   detect the local node (`:729-732`).
4. After releasing the lock, calls `esp_now_del_peer` then
   `esp_now_add_peer` with `channel = 0` (use current WiFi channel)
   and `ifidx = WIFI_IF_AP` (`:756-760`).
5. Emits a warning if the configured MAC appears to be an AP MAC
   (e.g. user pasted `ap_mac` instead of `base_mac`), by comparing
   the derived AP MAC against the local AP MAC (`:741-750`).

The `channel = 0` choice is intentional (comment at `:752-755`):
hardcoding channel 1 caused silent failures when the AP was on a
different channel.

### Multicast / broadcast

ESP-NOW has no native multicast. A `TBFT_ALL_REPLICAS` send is
implemented as a per-peer unicast fan-out inside `espnow_send_task`
(`tbft_transport_espnow.c:545-558`): for each peer in
`[0..num_replicas)`, skipping `local_id`, the task calls
`espnow_do_send` with a single shared `msg_id`. The receive side
treats each peer as a separate `(msg_id, src_mac)` tuple in
`reasm_find_or_alloc`, so multiple peers broadcasting the same
logical message do not collide.

## Host application responsibilities

### ESP-NOW

The host application must bring up WiFi **before** `Byz_init_replica`
calls `tbft_node_init`. Required order:

1. `esp_netif_init()`, default event loop
2. `esp_wifi_init(...)`
3. `esp_wifi_set_mode(WIFI_MODE_APSTA)` or `WIFI_MODE_STA`
4. `esp_wifi_start()`
5. `esp_now_init()` — registers the driver; required for
   `esp_now_register_recv_cb` to succeed
6. `Byz_init_replica(...)` — the BFT code path will then
   `tbft_transport_create` and `esp_now_register_recv_cb`
   (`tbft_transport_espnow.c:650`)

The `tbft_transport_create` retry loop in `src/tbft_node.c:54-67`
absorbs minor WiFi-bringup races, but a fully-untouched WiFi stack
will not recover.

### UDP

The host application must:

1. `esp_netif_init()` + default event loop + WiFi STA connect.
2. Provide a DHCP-acquired (or static) IP on `WIFI_STA_DEF` — the
   backend reads it via `esp_netif_get_handle_from_ifkey("WIFI_STA_DEF")`
   (`tbft_transport_udp.c:124`, `tbft_transport_espnow.c` is MAC-only).
3. Call `Byz_init_replica(...)` with the cluster's `mcast_ip` and
   `port` from the config file.

`local_id` is not derivable from the IP alone when multiple replicas
share a subnet. `tbft_transport_set_peer` resolves it by matching the
first peer whose IP equals the local WiFi STA IP; if no match is
found `local_id` stays at `-1` and the loopback-skip optimization
in `tbft_transport_send` is silently disabled.

## Buffer sizes

| Buffer | Where | Size | Source |
|--------|-------|------|--------|
| `tbft_transport_t.peers[]` (UDP) | `tbft_udp_t` static | `TBFT_MAX_NUM_REPLICAS + TBFT_MAX_NUM_CLIENTS` | `tbft_transport_udp.c:31` |
| `tbft_udp_t.peer_valid[]` | same | same | `tbft_transport_udp.c:32` |
| `tbft_espnow_t.peers[]` | `tbft_espnow_t` static | same | `tbft_transport_espnow.c:123` |
| `tbft_espnow_t.peer_ap_mac[][]` | same | same × 6 bytes | `tbft_transport_espnow.c:125` |
| Reassembly slots | `reasm[REASM_MAX_SLOTS]` | 8 × `TBFT_MAX_MESSAGE_SIZE` | `tbft_transport_espnow.c:135` |
| Reassembly message queue | `msg_queue` | `MSG_QUEUE_DEPTH = 16` entries × `recv_entry_t` | `tbft_transport_espnow.c:46, 627` |
| Reassembly entry payload | `recv_entry_t.payload[]` | `TBFT_MAX_MESSAGE_SIZE` | `tbft_transport_espnow.c:85` |
| Send queue | `send_queue` | `SEND_QUEUE_DEPTH = 8` entries × `send_entry_t` | `tbft_transport_espnow.c:47, 628` |
| Send entry buffer | `send_entry_t.buf[]` | `TBFT_MAX_MESSAGE_SIZE` | `tbft_transport_espnow.c:103` |
| Fragment packet | `pkt[]` in `espnow_do_send` | `sizeof(frag_hdr_t) + FRAG_MAX_PAYLOAD` | `tbft_transport_espnow.c:432` |
| Send task stack | FreeRTOS task | `SEND_TASK_STACK_SIZE = 8192` | `tbft_transport_espnow.c:53` |
| Recv buffer (caller) | `r->in_buf` | `TBFT_MAX_MESSAGE_SIZE` | `tbft_config.h:12-13` |

`TBFT_MAX_MESSAGE_SIZE` is the single most important compile-time
constant: it must accommodate the largest BFT message
(`New_key_bytes` for `n` replicas), and it is the upper bound on
reassembly and queue-entry sizes. With default Kconfig
(`TBFT_MAX_MESSAGE_SIZE = 2048`) most messages fit in a single
ESP-NOW fragment; multi-fragment code activates above 1470 bytes.

## Threading model

| Context | Code that runs there | Notes |
|---------|----------------------|-------|
| `tbft_replica_run()` task | `tbft_node_send` → `tbft_transport_send`; `tbft_node_recv` → `tbft_transport_recv` | The single BFT main loop. Both calls are non-blocking. |
| WiFi task | `espnow_recv_cb` (registered at `:650`) | Lock timeout is 5 ms (`tbft_transport_espnow.c:356`). Fragment past deadline is dropped. |
| WiFi task | `espnow_send_cb` (registered at `:657`) | Releases one TX credit per call (`:333`). |
| `tbft_send` FreeRTOS task | `espnow_send_task` (`:501-577`), `espnow_do_send` (`:415-499`) | Stack 8 KB, priority 5. The only place that calls `esp_now_send`. |
| UDP sender | `tbft_replica_run()` task | `sendto` is called directly from the BFT main loop. |

There is no ISR context in the transport layer. Both ESP-NOW
callbacks run as ordinary FreeRTOS tasks, which is why the code
uses `xSemaphoreTake` and `xQueueSend` directly
(`src/tbft_transport_espnow.c:356`, `:394`).

The ESP-NOW send path is fully decoupled from the BFT loop via the
`send_queue` + `send_task` design: the replica drops a message into
the queue (100 ms timeout) and returns immediately. This insulates
the protocol loop from ESP-NOW TX-queue stalls, which would
otherwise block the entire BFT main loop on a non-blocking socket.
